title: Set two weld-neck flanges on their riser stubs, two-holed to the plant centrelines
instruction: Fit-up on the two riser stubs: set each weld-neck flange on the stub it is bored for, neck down on the stub end and centred, and two-hole it to the plant centrelines painted on the floor around the stub. The small black circles on each flange's face are its bolt holes. Then let go of both flanges and move the grippers clear.
context: Pipefitters fitting up process piping set each flange on its pipe before it is tacked. The flange is 'two-holed': its bolt holes straddle the plant's principal centrelines and never sit on them unless the drawing asks for it, so that it mates with valves, instruments and the matching flange however the far end is laid out. On a vertical riser those are the plant north-south and east-west lines (Wermac, flange bolt hole orientation; the same convention as ASME B16.5 flanged fittings). Bolt counts are multiples of four and smaller pipe carries fewer bolts (Class 150: NPS 2 has 4, NPS 4 has 8), so what two-holing means depends on the flange in hand. A weld-neck flange is bored to its pipe and set neck down on the pipe end. Here two flanges of different sizes start with their holes on the lines, as an untrained hand would set them, and each fits only one of the two stubs.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A scaled fit-up bench for two vertical risers; plant north is +x (so plant west is +y). (1, 2) Riser stubs, fixed: two black steel pipe stubs standing upright on the table, each 60 mm tall with a flat end 60 mm above the table (the bore is not drawn): the small stub, 36 mm outside diameter, its axis at x 33.0 cm, y +15.0 cm; the large stub, 50 mm outside diameter, its axis at x 33.0 cm, y -15.0 cm. (3) Plant centrelines, fixed: around each stub, white paint 4 mm wide and 0.5 mm thick on the table, the north-south line along x and the east-west line along y, crossing at the stub's axis and running from the stub's surface out to 80 mm from its axis each way (x 25.0 to 41.0 cm; y +7.0 to +23.0 cm around the small stub, -23.0 to -7.0 cm around the large one). A white painted 10 x 10 mm square (0.5 mm thick) just past each north end, centred at x 41.7 cm, marks plant north. (4) 4-hole weld-neck flange, loose, 0.12 kg, solid aluminium painted steel grey: a disc 60 mm across and 12 mm thick on a neck 36 mm across and 10 mm tall below it, 22 mm tall overall; its neck matches the small stub. Painted black on its face, 0.5 mm thick: a bore disc 26 mm across in the middle and 4 bolt holes 8 mm across, equally spaced (90 degrees apart) on a 46 mm bolt circle. (5) 8-hole weld-neck flange, loose, 0.18 kg, the same material and paint: a disc 70 mm across and 12 mm thick on a neck 50 mm across and 10 mm tall, 22 mm tall overall; its neck matches the large stub. A bore disc 40 mm across and 8 bolt holes 7 mm across, 45 degrees apart on a 56 mm bolt circle, painted black on its face. Both flanges start lying neck down on the table, the 4-hole flange centred at x 21.0 cm, y +13.0 cm and the 8-hole flange at x 21.0 cm, y -13.0 cm, each with one bolt hole pointing along +x, so their holes lie on the centrelines' directions (the 4-hole flange's at 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees, the 8-hole flange's every 45 degrees from 0). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from both flanges' poses and both grippers (in a real trial: a rule, a square laid on the painted lines and a photo from above). A flange is 'seated' when all of these hold: (a) it is on the stub it is bored for: the 4-hole flange on the 36 mm stub, the 8-hole flange on the 50 mm stub (on the other stub it is not seated); (b) centred: its axis within 6 mm of the stub's axis, seen from above; (c) on the stub end: the centre of its neck's bottom within 3 mm of the stub end's height, face up, its axis within 5 degrees of vertical; (d) still: over the last 1 s neither the centre of its neck's bottom nor the centre of one of its holes moved more than 2 mm; (e) let go: no gripper's pad-tip point (midway between its finger tips) lower than 10 mm above the flange's highest point (its painted face when level) while within a finger's reach of the flange's axis horizontally, at any gripper yaw (half the finger gap plus 10 mm out and 20 mm across, plus the flange's radius and 5 mm: about 95 mm for the 4-hole flange and 100 mm for the 8-hole one, fully open). A seated flange is 'two-holed' when its bolt holes straddle the centrelines: with psi the angle seen from above from the north-south line (+x) to the line from the flange's axis to any one of its holes, psi modulo the hole pitch (90 degrees for 4 holes, 45 for 8) is within 8 degrees of 45 for the 4-hole flange (37 to 53) and within 7 degrees of 22.5 for the 8-hole flange (15.5 to 29.5). A flange with a hole on a centreline (psi modulo the pitch near 0) is not two-holed. With s the number of seated flanges (0 to 2) and t the number of those that are two-holed (0 to s): score = 0.25 s + 0.25 t. So 1.0 for s 2, t 2 (success; once held 1 s the trial ends); 0.75 for s 2, t 1 (for example the 4-hole answer copied onto the 8-hole flange, whose holes are then back on the lines); 0.5 for s 2, t 0 (both seated with their holes on the lines, as they start) or s 1, t 1; 0.25 for s 1, t 0; 0 for s 0 (nothing moved; the flanges swapped onto the wrong stubs; on the table; face down or on a rim; still held or still moving). Every outcome maps to exactly one score. Pushing cannot seat a flange: the stub ends are 60 mm up.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction; the stubs and lines are fixed. The flanges are scaled-down solid aluminium models, the two sizes drawn closer in diameter than ASME B16.5 sizes so a gripper can hold both; bolt holes and bores are painted, not drilled, and the flanges rest on the stub ends instead of being tacked. The bolt counts (4 and 8) and the straddle rule are unchanged, and the scored quantity is an angle, which scaling does not change.
reset_notes: Put the 4-hole flange back neck down on the table centred at x 21.0 cm, y +13.0 cm, and the 8-hole flange at x 21.0 cm, y -13.0 cm, each with one bolt hole pointing along +x (plant north), so all their holes lie on the centrelines' directions. The stubs and painted lines are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
